The other side of Authority is pressure; the original says that meeting Qing Yang, Tuo Luo, Di Kong or Di Jie it listens to slander and brings trouble on itself, both sides in the same star. Note that Authority does not mean promotion; the book's principles forbid inferring specific events from the transformations. Which layer it belongs to, birth year, decade or year, decides the timescale of that push.
sihua.權.full:
Authority is set off by the heavenly stem of the birth year. Book Two of the *Complete Book* lists it stem by stem: for the Yi stem, Tian Ji turns to Abundance, Tian Liang to Authority, Zi Wei to Recognition and Tai Yin to Obstruction. Book One records Master Xiyi as saying that the star of Authority is the spirit that holds the power to judge and decide: placed in the Life or Body Palace and meeting Recognition and Abundance, it brings command in war and office in peace.

The range of meaning this book allows is: driving forward, taking responsibility, the power to decide, pressure. Authority points to stepping in: this matter is yours to decide, and the price is that the consequences are yours too. It is more active than Abundance, and more tiring.

The original sets both sides down in the same passage: with Recognition it brings writing that surpasses its age; with Qing Yang, Tuo Luo, Di Kong or Di Jie it listens to slander, brings trouble on itself and meets official setbacks. These aren't two destinies but one force showing in two ways under different conditions: with support it leads, without support it strains.

This book never reads Authority as promotion, taking power or any specific event. Its principles forbid drawing conclusions from a single transformation, and forbid predicting events. Here Authority describes only a stance and its cost, not what you will meet.

Which palace Authority falls in decides what it pushes; which layer sets it off decides the timescale of the push.

One common misreading needs pointing out: Authority and forcefulness are not the same thing. When the old text speaks of holding the power to judge and decide, it means having a deciding part in a position, not being overbearing in character. Someone with Authority in the Partnership Palace may simply be used to making the calls in a relationship, not hard to live with. The book's principles already forbid reading meanings as judgements of character.

sihua.科.label: Recognition
sihua.科.summary: Recognition is set off by the heavenly stem of the birth year. The *Complete Book* records Master Xiyi as saying that the star of Recognition sits the examinations of the upper world and governs letters and writing. The meaning this book allows is presentation, order, being seen, having a proper name: Recognition speaks of something being properly arranged, put into words and ready to show. It is lighter in force than Abundance or Authority; the original says that even when the four malefics clash with it, it still brings wealth and honour, a tone more cushioning than driving. Note that Recognition does not mean passing exams or qualifications; the book's principles explicitly forbid such inferences. It is the lightest of the four transformations, often colouring rather than driving. For the Geng and Ren stems, the schools disagree about which star turns to Recognition, and the book states that disagreement.
sihua.科.full:
Recognition is set off by the heavenly stem of the birth year. Book Two of the *Complete Book* lists it stem by stem: for the Bing stem, Tian Tong turns to Abundance, Tian Ji to Authority, Wen Chang to Recognition and Lian Zhen to Obstruction. Book One records Master Xiyi as saying that the star of Recognition sits the examinations of the upper world and governs letters and writing: placed in the Life or Body Palace and meeting Authority and Abundance, it brings the honour of a high minister.

The range of meaning this book allows is: presentation, order, a proper name, being seen. Recognition points to something being sorted out and ready to show: not necessarily achieved, but clearly stated. The old writers described it with the image of letters and ink, and that fits well: Recognition is the step of writing down what was formless.

Recognition is the lightest of the four transformations. The original says that even meeting malign stars it makes a fine scholar, and that even when the four malefics clash with it, it still brings wealth and honour; the tone leans towards cushioning and a floor rather than driving forward. In reading, Recognition often plays a colouring role: it makes things look settled, but doesn't make them happen.

This book never reads Recognition as exams, qualifications or fame. Those are specific events, and the book's principles forbid inferring the outcome of events from a chart. Here Recognition describes a way of presenting, not results.

For the Geng and Ren stems, the schools' versions disagree about which star turns to Recognition. When this book discusses the transformations, it states that disagreement.

Among the three layers, Recognition's role is also distinctive. Abundance, Authority and Obstruction all change the direction of things; Recognition mostly changes how they look. The same matter, with Recognition, can be spoken of and put on the table; without it, it gets done quietly. That difference needs explaining when writing a book, or readers will mistake presentation for achievement.

sihua.忌.label: Obstruction
sihua.忌.summary: Obstruction is set off by the heavenly stem of the birth year. The *Complete Book* records Master Xiyi as saying that Obstruction is the spirit of meddling in too much: placed in the Life or Body Palace, nothing goes smoothly all one's life. The meaning this book allows is holding back, going back and forth, needing to carry: Obstruction points to something you can't put down and have to keep watching. It is neither calamity nor punishment. The old texts speak of Obstruction very harshly, and this book uses none of it: its principles forbid fatalistic verdicts and scaremongering, and state that a single Obstruction can go on a watch list but is not enough to judge caution or adversity. Which palace Obstruction falls in shows where your attention gets caught, not that something will go wrong there.
sihua.忌.full:
Obstruction is set off by the heavenly stem of the birth year. Book Two of the *Complete Book* lists it stem by stem: for the Gui stem, Po Jun turns to Abundance, Ju Men to Authority, Tai Yin to Recognition and Tan Lang to Obstruction. Book One records Master Xiyi as saying that Obstruction is the spirit of meddling in too much: placed in the Life or Body Palace, nothing goes smoothly all one's life; met in a minor period, a year falls short; in a ten-year stage, ten years of regret.

The range of meaning this book allows is: holding back, going back and forth, needing to carry. Meddling in too much is in fact far more accurate than later usage: Obstruction is the thing you can't put down and keep turning back to. It takes up attention and makes things take the long way round, but it isn't punishment, and it doesn't foretell calamity.

The old verdicts on Obstruction are extremely heavy: nothing goes smoothly all one's life, sure to stumble, even wealth turns out badly and no honours are won. This book uses none of that language. Its principles rule out fatalistic verdicts and scaremongering, and state that a single Obstruction can go on a watch list, but is not enough to judge caution or adversity, still less to predict losing money, ill health or a marriage ending.

In practice, Obstruction is most useful for showing where your attention gets caught. Obstruction in the Wealth Palace speaks of how much money matters to you, not of losing it; Obstruction in the Partnership Palace speaks of back-and-forth in a relationship, not of it ending. A palace's name is not an event, as the book's principles put it.

One more thing: Obstruction isn't wholly negative. Meddling in too much means caring, and caring is often exactly where a person is truly invested. Many patterns the old texts agree are fine have Obstruction at their core. So this book neither writes Obstruction as something to avoid nor, going the other way, dresses it up as a trial; both would be drawing conclusions for the reader.

This book has one rule for Obstruction: say clearly where it catches, then leave the judgement to the reader.

ju.水二局.label: Water Two Bureau
ju.水二局.summary: The Water Two Bureau has the smallest number of the Five-Element Bureaus. The bureau is set by the sound element (nayin) of the Life Palace's stem and branch: if that element is Water, it is the Water Two Bureau. The *Complete Book*'s verse on the sound elements of the sixty stem-branch pairs lists them pair by pair, such as Jia Shen and Yi You, water from a spring. The bureau decides two things at once: which position Zi Wei starts from, and at what age (by Chinese reckoning) the ten-year stages begin. The Water Two Bureau begins at two, the earliest of the five. Note that the bureau is only a starting point, not a measure of a good or bad life; the old texts never ranked the bureaus. This book records the bureau it uses on the book's colophon page, so readers can compare with other chart tools.
ju.水二局.full:
The Five-Element Bureau is set by the sound element (nayin) of the Life Palace's stem and branch. Book Two of the *Complete Book* sets the whole process out clearly: first find the Life Palace's heavenly stem with the five-tiger method, look up the sound element of the resulting stem-branch pair, then go to that bureau and find where Zi Wei starts from the birth day. Whatever the sound element, that is the bureau. The table of sound elements is in the same book's verse on the sixty stem-branch pairs; for Water, for example, Jia Shen and Yi You, water from a spring.

The two in Water Two has two uses. First, it is an index into the table of Zi Wei's starting positions: the same lunar birthday puts Zi Wei in different palaces under different bureaus. Second, it is the age, by Chinese reckoning, at which the ten-year stages begin: the Water Two Bureau starts its first stage at two, and moves on every ten years.

This means people of the Water Two Bureau start their stages earliest, and the years in which their stages change differ from other bureaus. When writing the ten-year stage chapters, this book marks the starting age and the bureau it is based on, so readers can match them up.

It should be said: the bureaus have no ranking. The old texts list five bureaus to fix a starting point, not to grade anyone. Reading two as little and six as plenty misunderstands the field. The only real distinction of the Water Two Bureau is its early start; everything else depends on what the chart holds.

A technical note to finish: the sound elements come from the stem-and-branch system of the *Yuan Hai Zi Ping* lineage. Zi Wei Dou Shu borrows them to set the bureau, while Four Pillars astrology uses them to read a person's element. The same table, two systems, two uses, which shouldn't be confused. This book lists the source of its sound elements and the bureau on the colophon page, so readers can compare with other chart tools; when they don't match, the difference usually lies in this step.

ju.木三局.label: Wood Three Bureau
ju.木三局.summary: The Wood Three Bureau comes from the Life Palace's stem and branch having Wood as their sound element; the *Complete Book*'s verse on the sixty stem-branch pairs gives examples such as Wu Chen and Ji Si, wood of the great forest. The bureau decides where Zi Wei starts and the age at which the ten-year stages begin: the Wood Three Bureau begins at three by Chinese reckoning. Note that there is no ten-year stage in the years before that, and this book writes no year chapter for them, because its principles require any conclusion about a year to have the decade layer behind it. The bureaus themselves have no ranking; the old texts list five only to fix a starting point. The bureau is the index for where Zi Wei falls, and when Zi Wei moves, all fourteen major stars move with it, so this step must not go wrong.
ju.木三局.full:
The Wood Three Bureau is set by the sound element of the Life Palace's stem and branch. Book Two of the *Complete Book* records the process: find the Life Palace's heavenly stem with the five-tiger method, look up the sound element of the stem-branch pair, then go to that bureau and find where Zi Wei starts from the birth day. Same steps: if the sound element is Wood, it is the Wood Three Bureau. The table is in the same book's verse on the sixty stem-branch pairs; for Wood, for example, Wu Chen and Ji Si, wood of the great forest.

The bureau has two uses: an index into the table of Zi Wei's starting positions, and the age at which the ten-year stages begin. The Wood Three Bureau starts its first stage at three by Chinese reckoning, the second at thirteen, and so on.

There's one detail this book cares about especially: in the years before the first stage begins, the chart has no decade layer. For the Wood Three Bureau, that means ages one and two by Chinese reckoning. The book's principles require any conclusion about a year to rest on three layers, birth chart, decade and year, so no year chapter can be written for those years: the engine returns nothing, and the reasoning never fills in the nearest stage. That's not a defect, it's a fact.

The bureaus have no ranking. Three is no better than two and no worse than six; it is simply a different starting point.

One more reminder: the starting age uses Chinese reckoning, not Western age. Chinese reckoning counts by lunar year, with the year of birth counting as one. This book's engine marks in its output that it uses Chinese reckoning, and that the year boundary is the first day of the lunar year rather than the start of spring; these two settings differ, and the year in which stages change can shift by one depending on them. This is one of the most common sources of disagreement between chart tools. This book records both settings on its colophon page.

ju.金四局.label: Metal Four Bureau
ju.金四局.summary: The Metal Four Bureau comes from the Life Palace's stem and branch having Metal as their sound element; the *Complete Book*'s verse on the sixty stem-branch pairs opens with Jia Zi and Yi Chou, metal in the sea. The bureau does two things: it fixes where Zi Wei starts, and the age at which the ten-year stages begin. The Metal Four Bureau begins at four by Chinese reckoning. Of the five bureaus, Metal Four sits in the middle, but that middle carries no meaning: a bureau is not a score, and the old texts list five only to place Zi Wei, with no bearing on good or bad. There is no decade layer in the three years before the first stage, and this book writes no year chapter for them; that is a requirement of its principles, not an omission.
ju.金四局.full:
The Metal Four Bureau is set by the sound element of the Life Palace's stem and branch. Book Two of the *Complete Book* sets out the steps: find the Life Palace's heavenly stem with the five-tiger method, pair it with the Life Palace's earthly branch, look up the sound element to set the bureau, then go to that bureau and find where Zi Wei starts from the birth day. The table is in the same book's verse on the sixty stem-branch pairs, which opens with Jia Zi and Yi Chou, metal in the sea.

The bureau decides two things. First, where Zi Wei falls: the same lunar birthday gives different positions for Zi Wei under the Water Two and Metal Four Bureaus, and when Zi Wei moves, all fourteen major stars on the chart move with it. Second, the age at which the ten-year stages begin, which for the Metal Four Bureau is four by Chinese reckoning.

Because the bureau moves the whole chart, it is also the step where chart-casting most easily goes wrong. The *Complete Book* itself adds a warning here: the numbers must not slip, for an error of a hair becomes a miss of a thousand miles. This book's engine has independent tests guarding this step, and records the bureau used on the book's colophon page, so readers can check it.

To repeat: the bureaus have no ranking, and four doesn't mean average.

On the gap before the first stage: the Metal Four Bureau has no ten-year stage between ages one and three by Chinese reckoning. Those years still have their yearly layer, but lack the decade layer. The book's principles state that reading a year needs birth chart, decade and year, and with one layer missing there isn't enough to set a direction, so for those years this book writes only observations, with no directional rating. The engine reports the empty layer as it is.

The settings for Chinese reckoning and the year boundary also affect the years in which stages change, and this book always states them.

ju.土五局.label: Earth Five Bureau
ju.土五局.summary: The Earth Five Bureau comes from the Life Palace's stem and branch having Earth as their sound element; the *Complete Book*'s verse on the sixty stem-branch pairs gives examples such as Wu Yin and Ji Mao, earth on the city wall. It decides where Zi Wei starts and the age at which the ten-year stages begin: the Earth Five Bureau begins at five by Chinese reckoning. The bureau is the step where chart-casting most easily goes wrong, because when Zi Wei moves, all fourteen major stars move with it; the *Complete Book* itself warns that an error of a hair becomes a miss of a thousand miles. The bureau itself has no bearing on good or bad. There is no decade layer in the four years before the first stage, and for those years this book writes only observations, with no direction. This book's engine has independent tests guarding this step.
ju.土五局.full:
The Earth Five Bureau is set by the sound element of the Life Palace's stem and branch. Book Two of the *Complete Book* records the full process: find the Life Palace's heavenly stem with the five-tiger method, combine it with the branch, look up the sound element to set the bureau, then go to that bureau and find where Zi Wei starts from the birth day. The table is in the same book's verse on the sixty stem-branch pairs; for Earth, for example, Wu Yin and Ji Mao, earth on the city wall.

The bureau's job is to set the starting point. Where Zi Wei falls is decided by the bureau together with the lunar birthday, and once Zi Wei is placed, the six stars of the Zi Wei group and the eight of the Tian Fu group follow by fixed relationships. So if the bureau is wrong, the whole chart is wrong; that's why the *Complete Book* adds its warning at this point.

The second job is the ten-year stages. The Earth Five Bureau starts its first stage at five by Chinese reckoning, and moves on every ten years. There is no decade layer in the four years before that, and this book writes no year chapter for them.

On the number five: it is a starting age, not a grade and not a measure of strength. The old texts never ranked the Five-Element Bureaus, and any reading of the bureau as the quality of a life is not what the *Complete Book* means.

There's also a practical disagreement to explain: the starting age uses Chinese reckoning, which counts by lunar year, with the year of birth counting as one. If another chart tool uses Western age, or puts the year boundary at the start of spring rather than the first day of the lunar year, the year in which stages change will differ by one. This book records both settings on its colophon page, so readers can match them up.

The sound elements come from the stem-and-branch system; Zi Wei Dou Shu borrows them to set the bureau, and uses them differently from Four Pillars astrology.

ju.火六局.label: Fire Six Bureau
ju.火六局.summary: The Fire Six Bureau comes from the Life Palace's stem and branch having Fire as their sound element; the *Complete Book*'s verse on the sixty stem-branch pairs gives examples such as Bing Yin and Ding Mao, fire in the furnace. The example the *Complete Book* gives for placing the Life Palace happens to be a Fire bureau: a person born in a Jia year with the Life Palace in Yin gets Bing Yin by the five-tiger method, whose sound element is fire in the furnace, and so goes to the Fire bureau to find where Zi Wei starts from the birth day. The Fire Six Bureau begins its stages at six by Chinese reckoning, the latest of the five, with no decade layer in the five years before. The bureaus have no ranking; the old texts list five only to fix a starting point, and any reading of the bureau as the quality of a life is not what the original means.
ju.火六局.full:
The Fire Six Bureau is set by the sound element of the Life Palace's stem and branch, and the worked example in Book Two of the *Complete Book* on placing the Life Palace happens to be a Fire bureau, so the source for this entry is especially complete. The original says: for someone born in a Jia year with the Life Palace in Yin, the five-tiger method gives Bing Yin for Jia and Ji years; its sound element is fire in the furnace, so go to the Fire bureau to find where Zi Wei starts from the birth day; if born on the first day of the first month, Zi Wei starts from the You position.

That passage walks through the whole chain once: year stem to the Life Palace's stem, the Life Palace's stem and branch to the sound element, the sound element to the bureau, and the bureau plus lunar day to Zi Wei's position. This book's engine follows exactly that order.

The Fire Six Bureau begins its stages at six by Chinese reckoning, the latest of the five. That means five years without a decade layer before the first stage, and no year chapter can be written for them, because the book's principles require any conclusion about a year to have the decade behind it. For those years the engine returns nothing, rather than filling in the nearest stage.

The same point holds: six doesn't mean strong, nor late. The bureau is only a starting point, and the old texts give it no meaning of good or bad.

The *Complete Book* leaves a warning at the end of this passage: the numbers must not slip, for an error of a hair becomes a miss of a thousand miles. That warning belongs at the bureau step for good reason: the bureau moves Zi Wei, Zi Wei moves the fourteen major stars, and one slip changes the whole chart. This book's engine has independent tests guarding this step, and records the bureau, Chinese reckoning and year-boundary settings together on the colophon page.
